sn37.3:1.3: An unmarried girl (_kumāribhūta_) under twenty was said to be not mature enough for full ordination ([pli-tv-bi-vb-pc71:1.11]()), which is the same age as for the monks. A _gihigatā_ of just twelve, however, might be ordained. _Gihigatā_ is explained as “gone to the place of a man” (_purisantaragatā_, [pli-tv-bi-vb-pc66:2.7]()) so it may well be the same as here, a girl who is married or, perhaps, pledged for marriage. This item precedes menstruation, which also suggests the age of twelve. While marriage was accepted at such an age, intercourse waited until after puberty (Manu 9.88).
